### G. YAHWEH’S VISIT TO SODOM (18:1–33)

#### 1. Abraham the host (18:1–15)

**C-V2R1-04** [18 · structure · dual roles · hospitality contrast]  
Hamilton: for a last time Abraham is given advance notice of Isaac’s birth while Yahweh’s entourage journeys to Sodom to inspect. Abraham appears in two roles in ch. 18: (1) polite, deferential host; (2) outspoken intercessor for Sodom. Blatant contrast between Abraham’s hosting (ch. 18) and Sodomites’ hosting of the same delegation (ch. 19).  
- Quote: “There is also a blatant contrast between how Abraham hosted his visitors (ch. 18) and how the Sodomites hosted the same delegation (ch. 19).” (L75)  
→ [[abraham]], [[lot]], [[genesis]], [[sarah]]

**C-V2R1-05** [18:1 · theophany · Mamre · heat of day]  
Yahweh reappears in the heat of the day as Abraham rests by the tent among trees at Mamre. Visit in hottest part of day contrasts with God’s “visit” to Adam in the cool of the day (Gen 3:8).  
- Quote: “The visit of Yahweh to Abraham in the hottest part of the day… contrasts with his ‘visit’ to Adam in another garden in the cool of the day (Gen. 3:8).” (L77)  
→ [[abraham]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-06** [18:2–3 · singular/plural · angels and deity]  
Shift singular↔plural is a feature of the section (detailed list vv. 2–33). Similar oscillation God/angels in ch. 19, 21:17–18, Judg 6, Judg 13. Scholarly accounts: (a) two intertwined variants (three vs one visitor); (b) Speiser—address group vs leader; (c) A. R. Johnson—oscillation one/many in Israelite conception of God; ʾĕlōhîm “both one and more than one, and on this concept the NT doctrine of trinitarianism is built.”  
- Quote: “ʾĕlōhîm is both one and more than one, and on this concept the NT doctrine of trinitarianism is built.” (L85, attributed to Johnson’s idea as Hamilton reports it)  
→ [[genesis]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-07** [18 · narrative style · progressive discovery]  
Typical Hebrew narrative: author first states from author’s perspective (v. 1: Yahweh appeared), then narrates how the character discovers it (vv. 2ff.). Parallel progression in ch. 19; cf. Moses’ face (Exod 34:29), burning bush (Exod 3:2), Job.  
- Quote: “The writer first describes what has happened from the author’s perspective (v. 1). Then he proceeds to narrate how the discovery was made by the one involved directly in the story (vv. 2ff.).” (L87)  
→ [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-08** [18:2 · three men · theophany form · anti-trinitarian eisegesis]  
Visitors simply “three men”; no form delineation; ch. 19 suggests trio is Yahweh + two messengers—not stated in ch. 18. Obscurity intentional (quote from Fretheim/related note n.26). When God appears in form, human form is characteristic. “This is the one theophany in the Abraham cycle in which Yahweh appears to Abraham with others at his side.” Older Christian interpreters equated three with Trinity—Hamilton rejects as reading “a considerable amount into the text.”  
- Quote: “Obviously, such a statement reads a considerable amount into the text, and forces on the text an interpretation the text itself will not yield.” (L91)  
→ [[genesis]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-09** [18:3–5 · hospitality · ANE custom · Hebrews 13:2]  
Emphasis: Abraham’s solicitude—water for feet, rest, food. Host responsible for guest’s needs and safety under his roof—explains Lot’s actions in ch. 19. Visitors accept and eat; Yahweh/angels conceal identity; Abraham does not know he is “entertaining angels unawares” (Heb 13:2). Eating is concession to Abraham’s ignorance while Yahweh is in guise of wayfarer (18:8; 19:3)—not diluted Yahwist story of God eating.  
- Quote: “The host is responsible for his guest’s needs and safety as long as the guest remains under his roof.” (L93)  
- Quote: “He does not know that he is ‘entertaining angels unawares’ (Heb. 13:2).” (L95)  
→ [[abraham]], [[lot]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-10** [18 · Ugaritic parallels · Keret · Aqhat · non-ritual hospitality]  
Hamilton quotes Keret and Aqhat food-to-gods scenes at length, then rejects easy comparison: (1) Abraham unaware of visitors’ identity; (2) childlessness motif forthcoming but does not dictate actions—Abraham acts as gentleman/gracious host, not ritual to reverse infertility.  
- Quote: “He is not engaging in any ritual action, nor has he any hidden motive.” (L193)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]]

**C-V2R1-11** [18:6–8 · extravagance · calf · Sarah in tent]  
Three seahs fine flour = large amount (cf. 1 Sam 25:18; 1 Kgs 18:32). Curds, milk, tender choice calf (vs kids of goats elsewhere). Abraham stands by while they eat—waiter and host. Sarah does not join; in tent. Irony: visitors know Sarah’s name; Abraham does not know who they are. Question “Where is your wife Sarah?” compared with “Where is Abel your brother?” (4:9)—Abraham more respectful than Cain.  
- Quote: “Perhaps the narrator makes a deliberate contrast between the three men who know who Sarah is and Abraham who does not know who they are.” (L201)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]]

**C-V2R1-12** [18:10–11 · promise specificity · menopause · zqn]  
Prior son promises nebulous; now specific: at this time next year. Narrator (not Abraham’s speech) states advanced age and menopause; root zqn thrice (vv. 11–13). Sternberg: narrator colors Sarah’s laughter; “the more natural her doubt, the stronger our sense of God’s supernatural prescience.”  
- Quote: “Sarah had reached menopause.” / narrator places “special emphasis on the ages of Abraham and Sarah by the three-time use of the root zqn.” (L61–63, L207)  
→ [[sarah]], [[isaac]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-13** [18:12–15 · Sarah’s laugh · unbelief · lying · name hint]  
Sarah’s shock less skeptical than Abraham’s (she does not fall on face). Yahweh rebukes via Abraham: “Why did Sarah laugh?” Yahweh rephrases her words, omitting Abraham’s age. Unbelief does not abort promise. Fear → lie “I did not laugh”; “A second sin is committed (lying) in an attempt to cover up a first sin (unbelief).” Ending provides “recondite hint of the name of the child.”  
- Quote: “A second sin is committed (lying) in an attempt to cover up a first sin (unbelief).” (L223)  
- Quote: “Yahweh is providing Sarah with a ‘recondite hint of the name of the child.’” (L225)  
→ [[sarah]], [[isaac]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-14** [18:14 · “Is anything too demanding for Yahweh?”]  
Rhetorical question shifts couple from limited resources to God’s limitless resources; promise reinforced by kāʿēṯ ḥayyâ + lammôʿēḏ. Parallel rhetorical questions frame units: this one and “Shall not he who judges all the earth give right judgment?” (v. 25).  
- Quote: “Yahweh’s question to Abraham is designed to shift the patriarchal couple’s obsession beyond their own hopeless situation and their own limited resources to the limitless resources of their God.” (L221)  
→ [[sarah]], [[abraham]], [[covenant]]

#### 2. Abraham the intercessor (18:16–33)

**C-V2R1-15** [18:16–33 · unit links · noise motifs]  
Uniting emphases: men arrive (v. 1) / prepare to depart (v. 16); start/end Mamre; host → bold inquisitor; dual rhetorical questions; Abraham will not arbitrate Yahweh/Sarah but places himself between Yahweh and Sodom; noise provokes Yahweh—Sarah’s laugh and Sodom’s groans.  
- Quote: “In both units it is some kind of noise that provokes Yahweh — Sarah’s laugh and Sodom’s groans.” (L273)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sin]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-16** [18:17–19 · confidant · covenant · yādaʿ · mišpāṭ]  
Vv. 17–19 not later addition (despite smooth skip)—omit them and lose God adopting Abraham as confidant and Abraham as Sodom’s intercessor. Mutual trust questions; both answered yes. Amos 3:7 parallel. Soliloquy of promises (first/only time patriarchal promises as soliloquy) underscores infallibility—God will not deceive himself. Motive: nations blessed in him (12:3); first time since ch. 12 (exc. 14) Abraham involved with a nation’s destiny; Sodomites “blessed” = have an intercessor (Isa 53:12). yāḏaʿ = covenanted/known: intimacy + possible treaty-technical “recognize as legitimate servant.” Contrast: Yahweh knows Abraham yet goes to Sodom to know (v. 21); vs Sodomites who want to “know” guests (19:5)—benign vs diabolical knowledge. Abraham to instruct family in “righteousness and justice” (mišpāṭ)—yet Abraham will ask if Yahweh himself practices mišpāṭ (v. 25). Prophetic roles: exhorter before intercessor. Conditionality occasionally heard amid unilateral covenant (cf. 17:1, 9–14; 22:15–18; 26:2–5).  
- Quote: “For I have covenanted with him so that he may instruct his sons and family-to-be to observe the way of Yahweh by practicing righteousness and justice” (L239, Hamilton’s translation of 18:19)  
- Quote: “In a context that overwhelmingly emphasizes the unilateral nature of the covenant with the patriarchs, the voice of conditionality and mutality is occasionally heard.” (L297)  
→ [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-17** [18:20–21 · cry · sin of Sodom · verification · anthropomorphism]  
zeʿāqâ/seʿāqâ: cry of oppressed (Exod 22:22–23; Cain’s blood; Egypt). Cry is the city’s own cry (subjective), not about the city. Sarna (quoted): “heinous moral and social corruption, an arrogant disregard of elementary human rights, a cynical insensitivity to the sufferings of others.” Ezek 16:49: pride, surfeit, ease, no aid to poor—not total explanation (Gen 19 will add) but major part: “Social immorality plays as large a role in the Sodom story as does sexual immorality.” Rejects Enuma elish/Atrahasis noise parallels as source (no insomnia; Babylonian noise lacks moral overtones). Yahweh’s descent = judicial fact-finding speech to Abraham (not soliloquy)—anticipates Abraham’s theodicy questions.  
- Quote: “Social immorality plays as large a role in the Sodom story as does sexual immorality.” (L307)  
- Quote: “It appears that sin is the cause, and the clamor of Sodom and Gomorrah is the result produced by this cause.” (L297)  
→ [[sin]], [[genesis]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-18** [18:22 · stand before · prophetic intercession · tiqqun scribal]  
“Stand before” can mark prophetic intercessory ministry (Jer 15:1, 19). Abraham precursor of mediating prophet. Reports Masoretic tradition of tiqqûnê sôferîm claiming original “Yahweh stood before Abraham”; Hamilton skeptical—versions lack support; Exod 17:6 untreated; 19:27 supports traditional “Abraham before Yahweh.”  
- Quote: “when Abraham stands before God he is a precursor of the mediating prophet.” (L313)  
→ [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-19** [18:23–33 · bargaining · remnant · mercy not challenge of guilt]  
Abraham: preserve ṣaddîq (v. 23) then city for remnant (vv. 24ff.). Lowers 50→45→40 by fives, then 40→30→20→10 by tens; stops at ten (no reason given). Does not challenge Sodom’s moral evaluation; does not urge Sodom’s repentance; turns to God for mercy. Pattern for Samuel, Elijah, Elisha, Job, Amos, Moses. Confidence: “Shall not he who judges all the earth give right judgment?”—challenge or testimony of integrity. Few innocent more determinative than many wicked—holy remnant as means of community preservation. Later prophets: Jer 5:1 affirms one righteous might spare Jerusalem; Jer 31 / Ezek 14, 18 challenge transferable merit—Hamilton quotes position that Ezek 14 rejects Gen 18’s theological presupposition (attributed, not adjudicated).  
- Quote: “Nowhere does Abraham challenge God’s evaluation of Sodom’s moral turpitude. That judgment is not up for debate. Nor does he at any point turn to Sodom to urge repentance. Rather, he turns to God to ask for divine mercy.” (L325)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sin]], [[covenant]]

#### NT Appropriation — Gen 18

**C-V2R1-20** [NT · 1 Pet 3:6 · Sarah “lord”]  
1 Pet 3:1–6: wives’ submissiveness/exemplary behavior for missionary purpose. Appeals to Gen 18:12 “my husband/lord is old” (LXX kyrios). Peter’s “obeyed” (aorist) points to specific incident 18:1–15. Wives like Sarah become her children; as Abraham father of faithful (Rom 4:11), Sarah mother of holy virtuous wife.  
- Quote: “Peter’s reference to Sarah’s obedience to Abraham is not mentioned per se in Genesis. But because Peter puts the word ‘obeyed’ in the aorist tense, he had a specific incident in mind, and Gen. 18:1-15 is that incident.” (L345)  
→ [[sarah]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-21** [NT · Heb 11:11 · Sarah’s faith · textual crux]  
Heb 11:11: first woman of faith in the chapter; Sarah (famous for skeptical laughter) as faith model—contrasts Paul (no Sarah-faith allusions). Textual/interpretative problems: Abraham vs Sarah as subject; “received power for deposition of seed” = male act. Solutions: excise “even Sarah”; dative reading; retain Sarah as subject (Tasker: paradoxical genuineness). Hamilton leans toward Sarah: “beyond season of life” more bold for woman past fertility; Hebrews may observe more faith in Sarah than Gen 18 narrator.  
- Quote: “It may be that the writer of Hebrews observes a bit more faith on Sarah’s part, as she reflects on the possibility of becoming pregnant, than does the narrator in Gen. 18.” (L365)  
→ [[sarah]], [[isaac]]

### H. ANNIHILATION OF SODOM AND GOMORRAH (19:1–38)

#### 1. Lot as host and guardian (19:1–11)

**C-V2R1-22** [19 · unity with 18 · not independent sources]  
Argues strongly against Gen 18 and 19 as originally independent later sutured: shared vocabulary (Van Seters: 17 similarities); day→evening, tree→house, tent-dwelling Abraham vs house-dwelling Lot; 40-mile journey Mamre–Sodom midafternoon→evening reinforces supernatural messengers; three emissaries → two sent ahead while Yahweh stays (18:22); Yahweh lingers with Abraham / Lot lingers unable to leave; potential destruction → actualized.  
- Quote: “We would argue most strongly against the position that views Gen. 18 and 19 as two originally independent narratives that were only subsequently sutured.” (L401)  
→ [[genesis]], [[abraham]], [[lot]]

**C-V2R1-23** [19:1 · malʾākîm · messengers not winged angels · Lot at gate]  
malʾākîm = “messengers” (one word for human/supernatural); Vulgate bifurcation angelus/nuntio arbitrary. Called “men” elsewhere → conceived as human beings, not winged. Location of Sodom uncertain (south favored via Zoar). Lot at gate—place of justice/business; gēr yet among leaders. Lot alone acknowledges newcomers; bows with face to ground—outdoes uncle in welcome.  
- Quote: “the writer of this story conceived of the messengers that appeared to Lot as human beings, not as winged, supernatural beings.” (L407)  
→ [[lot]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-24** [19:2–3 · Lot courteous but ignorant · meal]  
Lot courteous but ignorant of mission; offers lodging; persistent → guests accept. Parallel: Abraham persuades Yahweh re annihilation; Lot persuades messengers re lodging—but failed to redeem Sodomites by presence. Serves unleavened cakes himself (unlike Abraham assigning Sarah kitchen duties).  
- Quote: “While Lot shares his uncle’s penchant for courtesy, he does not share his uncle’s concern for Sodom’s future.” (L411)  
→ [[lot]], [[abraham]]

**C-V2R1-25** [19:4–5 · sin of Sodom · yādaʿ = sexual · not hospitality-only · not rape-only]  
First clear revelation of Sodom’s sin (13:13 was general). Rejects “know = become acquainted / hospitality violation only” as “wild and fanciful”—Lot’s offer of virgin daughters makes intercourse the issue. Four problems with “homosexual rape only” reading: (1) yāḏaʿ never “abuse/violate”; (2) OT rape language is seize/lie with/humble; (3) inconsistent sense of “know” v. 5 vs v. 8; (4) forces Lot to say “do not rape visitors—rape my virgin daughters.” “Clearly, then, the incident frowns on homosexual relations for whatever reason.” Still: Lot’s offer “unsuccessful, unheroic”; audience may be “relieved not to be among the daughters of Lot.”  
- Quote: “Clearly, then, the incident frowns on homosexual relations for whatever reason.” (L433)  
- Quote: “his action is unsuccessful, unheroic, and it ‘may even make the audience of the story relieved not to be among the daughters of Lot.’” (L433)  
→ [[sin]], [[lot]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-26** [19:6–8 · Lot as failed mediator · surrogacy theme · inexcusable]  
Lot mediates by compromise—offers daughters rather than raise moral conscience; willing to expose daughters, not himself. Links: (1) one group spared by presence of another (chs 18–19 theme); (2) daughters later reverse roles (vv. 30–38)—“One licentious act deserves another.” Oriental host-protection ethic (Aqhat son-list) frames dilemma but does not exonerate—actions “as inexcusable as those of Abraham in Egypt (ch. 12) and… Gerar (ch. 20).”  
- Quote: “One should not use this custom, however, to exonerate Lot. His actions are as inexcusable as those of Abraham in Egypt (ch. 12) and those that follow in Gerar (ch. 20).” (L439)  
→ [[lot]], [[abraham]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-27** [19:9–11 · gēr · blindness · Judg 19 parallel]  
Sodomites reject Lot as judge because gēr; threaten worse to Lot than to guests. Guests save Lot; sanwērîm = faulty vision not total physical blindness (cf. 2 Kgs 6:18–19)—cannot find door. Parallel Judg 19–20: same hospitality-assault type-scene; difference = supernatural guests prevent scenario. Canonical witness: sins of nations later practiced by Israelites (Benjamin).  
- Quote: “The sins of the nations became the sin of the chosen nation.” (L455)  
→ [[lot]], [[sin]]

#### 2–3. Sons-in-law; departure (19:12–22)

**C-V2R1-28** [19:12–14 · outcry link · ṣāḥaq · sons-in-law]  
Messengers not omniscient about Lot’s family. “Outcry” links 18:20–21; mob noise may be form of cry Yahweh hears. hātān: Hamilton prefers futuristic participle—“who were to marry.” Sons-in-law treat warning as clowning (ṣāḥaq)—same verb as Sarah’s laugh: both hear “ridiculous” announcements (pregnancy / destruction). Reasons for disbelief: message implausibility more than messenger, if parallel to Sarah.  
- Quote: “Both hear incredible announcements. She is to become pregnant; Sodom is to be destroyed. What Sarah and Lot’s sons-in-law hear is, in their judgment, ridiculous.” (L483)  
→ [[lot]], [[sarah]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-29** [19:15–22 · dawdling · mercy · Zoar · Lot as mini-Abraham]  
No reason yet given for sparing Lot (unlike Noah’s righteousness)—wait for v. 29. Lot dawdles; messengers grab him—“Yahweh being merciful.” Twice risk of being “swept away” (verb Abraham used 18:23–24). Lot bargains for Zoar (tiny place)—angel acquiesces, scales down overthrow of plain; Lot resembles Abraham of ch. 18 who scaled down judgment threshold. Etymology Zoar/miṣʿār. Rejects vv. 17–22 as intrusive independent etymology.  
- Quote: “In so speaking Lot resembles the Abraham of ch. 18.” (L531)  
- Quote: “Against his better judgment Lot is led to his only possible point of salvation.” (L521)  
→ [[lot]], [[abraham]]

#### 4. Doomsday (19:23–29)

**C-V2R1-30** [19:23–25 · sulphurous fire · from heaven · overthrow]  
Destruction begins at sunrise (daytime—Abraham can see smoke). Double tetragrammaton deliberate—not freak of nature: “from Yahweh in heaven.” māṭar third time in Genesis (2:5 life-bringing; 7:4 and here life-denying). wāʾēš as hendiadys “sulphurous fire.” Phrase “from Yahweh in heaven” resists pure earthquake naturalism; “overthrow” = fixed image for divine judgment (Westermann), not only earthquake. Vegetation included—totality.  
- Quote: “the disaster that struck Sodom and its environs was not a freak of nature. Rather, it was sent deliberately by Yahweh himself.” (L567)  
→ [[sin]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-31** [19:26 · Lot’s wife · pillar of salt]  
Looking back defies v. 17; motive not specified (not necessarily affection for city). “Before divine judgment there is only the possibility of being smitten or of escaping, but no third alternative” (von Rad, quoted). neṣîḇ “pillar” unique sense here; salty marl SW Dead Sea inspired Wis 10:7 and Josephus traditions.  
- Quote: “She lost her life for only one reason: because she overtly ignored the directive of v. 17” (L577)  
→ [[lot]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-32** [19:27–29 · Abraham spectator · Lot spared for Abraham]  
Only chapter in Abraham cycle where Abraham appears but says nothing—mediator reduced to spectator. Abraham does not yet know Lot survived. v. 29: Lot spared because God “was mindful of Abraham”—undeserving individual spared because of another. Exactly the issue of ch. 18 dialogue: Abraham is to Lot what the hypothetical remnant would have been to Sodom.  
- Quote: “An individual who does not deserve to be spared (Lot) is spared because of another (Abraham).” (L587)  
- Quote: “Abraham is to Lot what the hypothetical righteous remnant (50, 45, 40, 30, 20, 10; ch. 18) would have been to Sodom.” (L587)  
→ [[abraham]], [[lot]], [[covenant]]

#### 5. Lot and his daughters (19:30–38)

**C-V2R1-33** [19:30–38 · incest · Moab/Ammon · knowledge theme · major theme restated]  
Lot fears Zoar → cave. Daughters: no man on earth (hyperbolic/local). Motive = progeny, not orgy—still objectionable. Role reversal of v. 8. Lot unaware (yāḏaʿ)—knowledge theme: Sodomites wanted to know guests; Lot does not know daughters. Moab “water/seed of father”; Ben-ammi “son of my kinsman”; “of today” extension formula. Third illustration of major theme of chs 18–19: (1) guilty spared for innocent; (2) Lot spared for Abraham’s covenant; (3) Moab/Ammon exist because of Abraham’s progeny (two daughters of Israel/Lot).  
- Quote: “Earlier the father was willing to use his daughters for sexual purposes without their consent. Now they will use their father for sexual purposes without his consent.” (L623)  
- Quote: “Thus we find a third illustration of a major theme in chs. 18—19” (L643, then the three points)  
→ [[lot]], [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[sin]]

#### NT Appropriation — Gen 18:16–19:38

**C-V2R1-34** [NT · Matt/Luke judgment · days of Lot · 2 Pet/Jude · Rev 11:8]  
(1) Matt 10:15; 11:20–24; Luke 10:12–15: more tolerable for Sodom than rejecting towns; Capernaum juxtaposed with Sodom (Matthew fullest). (2) Matt 24 / Luke 17: days of Noah (+ Lot in Luke)—emphasis on routineness then sudden catastrophe, not primarily Sodom’s sinfulness. (3) 2 Pet 2:6–8; Jude 7: Sodom as hotbed of immorality; Peter calls Lot “righteous”—Hamilton notes Gen 18–19 makes that adjective hard; Peter uses Lot as model who survived evil surroundings; “righteous” grounded in Abraham’s intercession logic (ten ṣaddîqîm) and Lot’s deliverance, not in whitewashing Lot. (4) Rev 11:8: great city allegorically Sodom and Egypt—rejection of messengers, rebellion, total judgment; connects to Jerusalem.  
- Quote: “Nothing in Gen. 18—19 makes the application of that adjective to Lot appropriate.” (re “righteous,” L681)  
- Quote: “Because Abraham made his case not on the grounds on kinship… but on the grounds of righteousness, and because Lot is delivered from judgment, Peter has no hesitancy in applying the adjective ‘righteous’ to Lot.” (L685)  
→ [[lot]], [[sin]], [[abraham]]

---

### I. ABRAHAM AND SARAH IN GERAR (20:1–18)

**C-V2R1-35** [20 · context with 18–19 · not only doublet of 12]  
Source criticism divorces chs 18–19 (J) from 20 (E); Hamilton stresses immediate-context links: vulnerable female (Lot’s daughters / Sarah); protection of male; judgment; “would God destroy innocent?” (Abraham 18 / Abimelech 20:4); gēr (19:9; 20:1); Abraham’s intercession (18:23–33; 20:17); time frames reverse (day→night vs night→day); cities outside future Israel’s land.  
- Quote: “What has gone unnoticed is the significance of ch. 20 to its immediate context.” (L727)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]], [[lot]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-36** [20:1–2 · second wife-sister · not mere doublet · postcovenant failure]  
From Mamre/Sodom vista to Negeb between Kadesh and Shur; family at Gerar while Abraham in Sinai region. Differs from ch. 12: no famine, no flattery of wife (Sarah now ~90 vs ~65), no prejudging Gerarites, more spontaneous. Refuses to call ch. 20 mere doublet: same person can stoop twice; postcovenant Abraham still like precovenant—moments of greatness intermingled with shortsightedness. Points to new-covenant hope (Jer 31; Ezek 36; Joel) for consistent covenant life; NT 1 Cor; discusses Rom 7 as unregenerate-under-law reading (logical not psychological order).  
- Quote: “If one views them as two separate events, then the Scriptures are showing that the postcovenant Abraham, for all his spiritual maturation (e.g., Gen. 15:6), is still much like the precovenant Abraham.” (L733)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]], [[covenant]]

**C-V2R1-37** [20:3–7 · dream · theodicy · prophet as intercessor · adultery vs God]  
First of four Genesis outsider dream-revelations (also Laban, butler/baker, Pharaoh)—warning dreams. Universal obligation re adultery; even ignorance has consequences. Apparent adultery here vs (probably) actual in ch. 12. Abimelech: “Innocent folk would you slay?”—parallel Abraham. gôy ṣaddîq = nation/people, not only king. God restrained Abimelech from touching Sarah—sin would be “against me.” First use of “prophet” (nābîʾ) in Bible: role = intercessor (“he will pray for you”). Duplicity did not disqualify Abraham as interceding prophet.  
- Quote: “This is the first use of prophet in the Bible. The role of the prophet here is that of intercessor: he will pray for you.” (L763)  
- Quote: “Abraham’s duplicity apparently did not disqualify him from functioning as an interceding nāḇî’.” (L763)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]], [[covenant]], [[sin]]

**C-V2R1-38** [20:8–18 · Abimelech exemplary then unmasked · half-sister claim · closed wombs · irony]  
Structure: problem (potential death) → God/Abimelech dialogue → Abraham/Abimelech dialogue → solution (barrenness reversed). Abimelech open vs Abraham’s subterfuge; courtiers “afraid” (yirʾû) undercuts Abraham’s “no fear of God” claim. Abraham’s defenses: false assumptions, casuistry (half-sister—genealogy silent; may be fabrication), incriminates God (“wander”) and Sarah (standing agreement; command not request). Gifts = compensation (cf. Middle Assyrian law); invitation to stay vs Pharaoh’s expulsion. “Covering of the eyes” foil for Sarah’s reputation. Abraham prays → Philistine women conceive while Sarah still barren (irony; ʿāṣar as in 16:2). Character reversal: Abimelech looks exemplary 16/18 verses then unmasked—only God’s restraint, not moral vigor, prevented adultery; order of judgment delayed vs ch. 12.  
- Quote: “Abraham will do everything except tell the truth.” (L815)  
- Quote: “Only the restraining providence of God, rather than any moral vigor on Abimelech’s part, deterred Abimelech from sleeping with Sarah.” (L849)  
→ [[abraham]], [[sarah]], [[sin]], [[covenant]]

### J. ISAAC AND ISHMAEL (21:1–34)

#### 1. Birth of Isaac (21:1–7)

**C-V2R1-39** [21:1–7 · visit · naming · circumcision · ṣeḥōq as “joke”]  
Yahweh “visited” (pāqaḏ) Sarah—deliberate third “appearance” after three men and two men; mercy from infertility (cf. Hannah, Elizabeth)—not divine sexual paternity myth. v. 1 poetry/chiasm, not needless J/P doublet. Fulfillment of 17:16; 18:10–14; focus on Abraham’s advanced age. Abraham names Isaac (God’s prior choice 17:19) and circumcises day 8—obedient not euphoric. Isaac “he laughs” without contextual etymology (unlike Ishmael). Sarah: “God has made a joke of me” (ṣeḥōq)—consistent with 17:17; 18:12–15 if “joke,” not pure joy; wishes “sons” plural not only son.  
- Quote: “Yahweh then visited Sarah as he said he would; Yahweh did for Sarah as he promised he would.” (L861, Hamilton’s translation)  
- Quote: “If Abraham is understandably euphoric at this moment in his life, such a feeling must not be allowed to lull the father into indifference with regard to his spiritual obligations to his son.” (L887)  
→ [[isaac]], [[sarah]], [[abraham]], [[covenant]]

#### 2. Expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael (21:8–21)

**C-V2R1-40** [21:8–21 · against simple E//J doublet · Ishmael’s age]  
Standard criticism: 21:8–21 = E parallel to J 16. Hamilton will “call into question” age-confusion argument: Hebrew does not put teenage Ishmael on mother’s back—nāṯan = entrust child + put provisions on shoulder; šālaḵ = lower/deposit with dignity, not “cast” infant.  
- Quote: “Only if one follows the LXX does he encounter the idea that Abraham placed Ishmael (a teenage adolescent!) on his mother’s back.” (L967)  
→ [[ishmael]], [[isaac]], [[abraham]], [[genesis]]

**C-V2R1-41** [21:9–13 · meṣaḥeq · inheritance · gāraš · God sides with Sarah]  
Sarah sees Ishmael “playing” (Piel ṣāḥaq)—options: athletic display, stealing spotlight, sexual sense, “Isaac-ing” (claiming equal status); LXX/Vulg add “with Isaac”; Paul Gal 4:29 “persecuting.” Real issue v. 10: inheritance—slave woman’s son not share with Isaac. gāraš as expel/divorce-term; shift šipḥâ→ʾāmâ = Hagar’s advanced status. Cuneiform: slave’s son can claim inheritance—Sarah may urge illegal act. Abraham upset “on account of his son.” God: do what Sarah says—“through Isaac… descendants shall be named”; also make nation of slave’s son. God calls Ishmael naʿar; parents yeleḏ—minimizes sonship. “God using the wrath of a human being to accomplish his purposes.”  
- Quote: “She is disturbed not by Ishmael’s behavior (v. 9), but by the possibility that this ben-ʾāmâ is in a position, legally, to share the inheritance with Isaac.” (L949)  
- Quote: “Here is an instance of God using the wrath of a human being to accomplish his purposes.” (L957)  
→ [[ishmael]], [[isaac]], [[sarah]], [[abraham]], [[covenant]]

**C-V2R1-42** [21:14–21 · send off · wilderness · well · type-scene with 22 · Paran · Egyptian wife]  
Abraham rises early; bread/water; šālaḥ (send off) less harsh than gāraš. Hagar wanders (tāʿâ—same root Abraham used 20:13). Prayer-wish: “Do not let me see the child die.” God hears lad’s cry (Ishmael etymology); messenger from heaven (rare; cf. 22:11, 15). Promise of great nation after ordeal. God opens eyes to well—parallel Abraham eyes/ram (22) type-scene (Alter). God with the lad; bowman; wilderness of Paran; mother gets Egyptian wife. Unit structure: v. 8 Isaac; vv. 9–21 Ishmael.  
- Quote: “With the life of a child in danger God opens Hagar’s eyes… Similarly… Abraham lifts up his eyes… and sees… a ram” (L989)  
→ [[ishmael]], [[isaac]], [[abraham]]

#### 3. Conflict over a well / Beer-sheba (21:22–34)

**C-V2R1-43** [21:22–34 · covenant with Abimelech · ḥeseḏ · seven ewes · Beer-sheba etymology]  
Abimelech + Phicol: “God is with you”; requests oath against dealing falsely (šāqar)—ironical after ch. 20 deception; ḥeseḏ based on precedent of Abimelech’s prior loyalty, not superior force. Abraham’s well seized; complaint without reported legal resolution—covenant groundwork instead. Seven ewe lambs = witness Abraham dug the well. Beer-sheba: Hamilton renders kî in v. 31 as temporal “when,” not “because,” avoiding dual “seven/oath” source split—ʿal-kēn connects seven lambs to name. Planting tamarisk; invokes Yahweh ʾēl ʿôlām. Defends “Philistine” against pure anachronism: patriarchal Philistines peaceful under “king” vs later bellicose under “lords”—first vs last Sea People waves.  
- Quote: “Will their relationship in the future, asks Abimelech, be determined by šeqer, ‘falsehood,’ or by ḥeseḏ, ‘loyalty’?” (L1043)  
- Quote: “v. 31b does not tell why Abraham gave this place the name Beer-sheba, but when Abraham gave it this name.” (L1071)  
→ [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[genesis]]

#### NT Appropriation — Gen 16; 21 / Gal 4

**C-V2R1-44** [NT · Gal 4:21–5:1 · allegory Hagar/Sarah]  
Paul allegorises Hagar/Sarah as two simultaneous (not successive) covenants—not old vs new. Flesh vs promise (not yet Spirit until v. 29). Hagar → Sinai / present Jerusalem; Sarah → Jerusalem above. Quotes Isa 54:1. Application: believers called like Isaac to freedom. Rejects reading as demeaning attack equating Judaism with Hagar—Paul confronts Gentile Galatians tempted to reverse from Spirit to flesh (e.g., force circumcision); that would be Ishmael “persecuting” Isaac again.  
- Quote: “Hagar and Sarah represent two covenants that are simultaneous and not successive, and hence the possibility is eliminated that Paul is contrasting the old covenant with the new covenant.” (L1099)  
- Quote: “Believers, says Paul, must choose between being Ishmael people (i.e., those who live by the flesh) or Isaac people (i.e. those who live by the Spirit).” (L1107)  
→ [[isaac]], [[ishmael]], [[sarah]], [[covenant]]
